name: Greedy trap (unit Day 4)
description: A constructed counterexample for the heuristic-vs-exact lesson: the smallest network we could find on which the greedy budget interdictor is strictly worse than the exhaustive one. Baseline throughput is 140 (80 down s->A->D->t, 30 down s->B->C->t, 30 down s->C->t). With a budget of two lanes, exhaustive search removes C->t and D->t -- the only two lanes into t -- and drives throughput to 0. Greedy cannot see that pair: it opens with the most damaging single lane, s->A at 80, and is left with a network whose best remaining removal is worth only 30, stalling at 30. That gap is the sentence Day 4 is built on -- greedy fails when the best blockade isn't where the biggest single lane is. Nodes are named in Day 2's abstract register so this reads as a constructed instance rather than a theater; the theater cannot demonstrate this divergence and cannot be edited into demonstrating it. NOTE: the order of the edges array is load-bearing -- three lanes tie at damage 80 and greedy's tie break is first-in-file, so a reordering that puts D->t first lets greedy reach 0 too and erases the lesson. See test_trap_edge_order_preserves_the_divergence.
